Subject: Review: Vantorre CX-10 10-tray electric combi (order CM-88213)

3/5 — the service side was good, the unit itself wasn't.

Unit: Vantorre CX-10 10-tray electric combi, refurbished 2021, s/n VT21-30877, order CM-88213, delivered and commissioned 14/09/2026, $14,800 inc GST. Warranty registered to 14/03/2027.

The temperature side got fixed properly. Core probe was reading low: combi display 63°C against a ThermoPen reading 70°C in a lamb shoulder, reproduced twice, raised with Kelsall on 03/10. Recalibrated at the 06/10 visit and now within 1°C.

The steam generator is the problem. Error log shows E34 — steam generator low water level — nine times between 14/09 and 22/09, when SR-1190 replaced the water level sensor; inlet pressure checked OK at 320 kPa. SR-1236 on 06/10 found the generator heavily scaled, descaled and flushed.

Our supply is 15 mg/L as CaCO3, which the water company rates among the softest in the country. A combi steam generator doesn't build that scale in three weeks on 15 mg/L water, and the listing states the generator was descaled and pressure tested before delivery — so the scale appears to have arrived with the unit.

24/10, 6.10pm: E34 locked us out mid-service, full book of 60 covers. Lamb finished on the stove and deck oven, pork belly 86'd, cost absorbed. Another E34 and further scale on 27/10, invoiced at $280 + GST ($308) as a non-warranty site water issue, on a unit six weeks old with warranty running to 14/03/2027.

Credit to the service side — both attendances were quick and the probe was sorted on the day. But other kitchens should know what they're signing for before dropping $15k on a unit that arrives with the generator already scaled.
